question: How many breakfast cereals have a Nutri-Score of A?
facts: 1,323 breakfast cereals have Nutri-Score A.

truth.query: select count(*) as n from serving.products where category_id = 'breakfast-cereals' and nutriscore_grade = 'a'

question: How many breakfast cereals have under 5 g of sugar per 100 g and no colour additives?
facts: 3,347 breakfast cereals have under 5 g sugar per 100 g and no colour additive.

truth.query: select count(*) as n from serving.products p where category_id = 'breakfast-cereals' and sugars_100g < 5 and not exists (select 1 from serving.additives a where a.additive_id = any(p.additive_ids) and a.function ilike '%color%')

question: How many sodas and soft drinks are in LabelLens?
facts: There are 25,293 sodas and soft drinks.

truth.query: select count(*) as n from serving.products where category_id = 'sodas'

question: What share of candy and chocolate products with a NOVA group are ultra-processed (NOVA 4)?
facts: About 95.5% of candy and chocolate products with a NOVA group are NOVA 4.

truth.query: select round(100.0 * count(*) filter (where nova_group = 4) / count(*), 1) as pct from serving.products where category_id = 'candy-chocolate' and nova_group is not null

question: What is the median sugar content of yogurts and dairy desserts per 100 g?
facts: The median is about 8.9 g of sugar per 100 g.

truth.query: select round(percentile_cont(0.5) within group (order by sugars_100g)::numeric, 1) as m from serving.products where category_id = 'yogurt' and sugars_100g is not null

question: How many products list xanthan gum (E415)?
facts: 39,492 products list xanthan gum (E415).

truth.query: select count(*) as n from serving.products where 'en:e415' = any(additive_ids)

question: Which additive appears in the most products?
facts: Citric acid (E330) appears in the most products, 100,764.

truth.query: select a.e_number, a.name, count(*) as n from serving.products p, unnest(p.additive_ids) x(id) join serving.additives a on a.additive_id = x.id group by 1, 2 order by 3 desc limit 1

question: How much sugar per 100 g does the product with barcode 0016000275287 have?
facts: Barcode 0016000275287 is Cheerios (Cheerios).
It has about 5.1 g of sugar per 100 g.

truth.query: select name, brand, round(sugars_100g::numeric, 1) as s from serving.products where code = '0016000275287'

question: What is the Nutri-Score and NOVA group of barcode 0049000042566?
facts: Barcode 0049000042566 is Coca-Cola Zero Sugar.
Its Nutri-Score is C.
Its NOVA group is 4.

truth.query: select name, nutriscore_grade as g, nova_group as nova from serving.products where code = '0049000042566'

question: Which additives does Nacho Cheese Flavored Doritos (barcode 0028400516464) list?
facts: It lists 8 additives.
One of them is Tartrazine.
One of them is Sunset yellow FCF.
One of them is Allura red.

truth.query: select a.name from serving.products p, unnest(p.additive_ids) with ordinality x(id, i) join serving.additives a on a.additive_id = x.id where p.code = '0028400516464' order by x.i

question: What are the first three ingredients of Lucky Charms, barcode 0016000123991?
facts: The first three ingredients are Oats, Sugar, Oat flour, in that order.

truth.query: select i.name from serving.products p, unnest(p.ingredient_ids) with ordinality x(id, k) join serving.ingredients i on i.ingredient_id = x.id where p.code = '0016000123991' order by x.k limit 3

question: How many products in LabelLens have no Nutri-Score?
facts: 600,195 products have no Nutri-Score.

truth.query: select count(*) as n from serving.products where nutriscore_grade is null

question: Which food category has the highest median sugar per 100 g?
facts: Candy and chocolate has the highest median sugar, about 50 g per 100 g.

question: How many chips, crackers and salty snacks have more than 1.5 g of salt per 100 g?
facts: 26,407 salty snacks have more than 1.5 g salt per 100 g.

truth.query: select count(*) as n from serving.products where category_id = 'salty-snacks' and salt_100g > 1.5

question: What is the median protein per 100 g of supplements and protein powders?

facts: 9,328 juices and fruit drinks have more than 10 g sugar per 100 g.

question: Which well-known products contain mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids (E471)?
facts: Creamy Peanut Butter (Jif) contains E471.

truth.query: MATCH (p:Product)-[:CONTAINS]->(:Additive {id: 'en:e471'}) OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[:MADE_BY]->(b:Brand) RETURN p.name AS name, b.name AS brand ORDER BY p.rank LIMIT 3

question: Which well-known breakfast cereals contain tocopherols (E306)?
facts: Ancient Grains Probiotic Granola contains tocopherols.
Pumpkin Seed + Flax Granola contains tocopherols.
Lightly Sweetened Maple Berry Blend Cereal contains tocopherols.

truth.query: MATCH (p:Product {category: 'breakfast-cereals'})-[:CONTAINS]->(:Additive {id: 'en:e306'}) RETURN p.name AS name ORDER BY p.rank LIMIT 3

question: Which breakfast cereals have the most ingredients in common with Lucky Charms, barcode 0016000123991?
facts: Frosted Oat Cereal With Marshmallows shares 26 ingredients with it.
Count Chocula shares 22 ingredients with it.
Chocolate Lucky Charms shares 22 ingredients with it.

truth.query: MATCH (p:Product {code: '0016000123991'})-[:HAS_INGREDIENT]->(i)<-[:HAS_INGREDIENT]-(o:Product) WHERE o.category = p.category AND toLower(o.name) <> toLower(p.name) WITH o, count(i) AS shared RETURN o.name AS name, shared ORDER BY shared DESC, o.rank LIMIT 3

question: Which salty snacks have ingredients most like Nacho Cheese Flavored Doritos, barcode 0028400516464?
facts: Nacho Cheese shares 26 ingredients with it.
Doritos minis nacho cheese shares 25 ingredients with it.

truth.query: MATCH (p:Product {code: '0028400516464'})-[:HAS_INGREDIENT]->(i)<-[:HAS_INGREDIENT]-(o:Product) WHERE o.category = p.category AND toLower(o.name) <> toLower(p.name) WITH o, count(i) AS shared RETURN o.name AS name, shared ORDER BY shared DESC, o.rank LIMIT 2

question: Which categories sit alongside breakfast cereals under the same parent category?
facts: The parent category is Bread, cereals and grains.
Bread and tortillas is a sibling category.
Pasta, rice and grains is a sibling category.

truth.query: MATCH (:Category {id: 'breakfast-cereals'})-[:CHILD_OF]->(p:Category)<-[:CHILD_OF]-(s:Category) WHERE s.id <> 'breakfast-cereals' RETURN p.name AS parent, s.name AS name ORDER BY s.name

question: What are the most common additives in breakfast cereals in the graph?
facts: Tocopherol-rich extract is among the most common.
Sodium carbonates is among the most common.
Sodium hydrogen carbonate is among the most common.

truth.query: MATCH (:Category {id: 'breakfast-cereals'})<-[:IN]-(p:Product)-[:CONTAINS]->(a:Additive) RETURN a.name AS name, a.id AS id, count(DISTINCT p) AS n ORDER BY n DESC, id LIMIT 3

question: What is carrageenan and why is it in yogurt?
facts: In short: A gel-forming substance extracted from red seaweed, used to thicken, stabilize and hold ingredients evenly mixed in foods.

truth.query: select name, explainer from serving.additives where additive_id = 'en:e407'

question: Why is lecithin used in chocolate?
facts: In short: Lecithins are a mixture of phospholipids, fatty substances usually extracted from soybeans, sunflower seeds, or eggs.

truth.query: select name, explainer from serving.additives where additive_id = 'en:e322'

question: What does xanthan gum do in food?
facts: In short: Xanthan gum is a polysaccharide produced by fermenting sugar with a bacterium.

truth.query: select name, explainer from serving.additives where additive_id = 'en:e415'

question: What is sodium benzoate?
facts: In short: The sodium salt of benzoic acid, used as a preservative to slow the growth of molds, yeasts and bacteria in acidic foods.

truth.query: select name, explainer from serving.additives where additive_id = 'en:e211'

question: What is annatto?
facts: In short: Annatto is a natural orange-yellow color obtained from the seeds of the achiote tree, used to tint cheeses, butter, and other foods.

truth.query: select name, explainer from serving.additives where additive_id = 'en:e160b'

question: Why is citric acid added to drinks?
facts: In short: A weak organic acid found naturally in citrus fruits, used to add tartness and to act as an antioxidant and sequestrant in foods.

truth.query: select name, explainer from serving.additives where additive_id = 'en:e330'

question: What is TBHQ?
facts: In short: A synthetic form of hydroquinone, used as an antioxidant to slow the oxidation of fats and oils in foods.

truth.query: select name, explainer from serving.additives where additive_id = 'en:e319'

question: What are mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids?
facts: In short: Mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids are fat-derived emulsifiers made by partially reacting glycerol with edible fatty acids.

truth.query: select name, explainer from serving.additives where additive_id = 'en:e471'

question: What is maltodextrin?
facts: In short: A white powder made by partially breaking down corn, rice, wheat or potato starch into short chains of sugar units.

truth.query: select name, explainer from serving.ingredients where ingredient_id = 'en:maltodextrin'

question: What is high fructose corn syrup?
facts: In short: A liquid sweetener made from corn starch that has been processed so that part of its glucose is converted to fructose, giving a sweet, stable syrup.

truth.query: select name, explainer from serving.ingredients where ingredient_id = 'en:high-fructose-corn-syrup'
